rationale: The analysis identifies the correct causal chain: downstream rate-limit cut (E4) → 429s (E5) → retry backoff drives latency (C4→C1), with the cache hit-rate drop (E2) correctly demoted to a downstream symptom of retry cache-bypass headers (E7) rather than a cause, explicitly supported by the discriminating evidence in E6 (non-429 requests unaffected regardless of cache hit/miss) and the healthy cache service (E3). All four required findings are present (rate-limit→429/retry, retries→latency, cache decline as downstream retry effect, restoration ending the incident), and the forbidden claim (cache degradation as cause) is explicitly and repeatedly rejected (C7, C8, CF6). Every claim cites specific evidence IDs with no outside facts introduced; the counterfactuals (especially CF2, CF3, CF6) demonstrate genuine causal-structure reasoning rather than restating evidence. Confidence levels are well calibrated — high on the well-established core chain (matching the case's low stated uncertainty), medium/flagged as open for legitimately unresolved points (why the rate limit changed, backoff-vs-downstream-work split, tail latency), each paired with a concrete resolving-evidence description. Actions correctly prioritize the rate-limit/retry mechanism (A1 explicitly rules out cache-focused remediation), propose reasonable secondary mitigations (decoupling cache-bypass from retries, honoring Retry-After, coordinating on rate-limit changes) without weakening any protective control or exceeding the evidence. No unsupported, harmful, or outside-evidence claims were found.
